## Phase 1 — PROVEN root cause (rebar-debug)

### Step 0 sweep
- `Step 0(a): duplicates none.` The only near-match is `unreal-milky-sloth` /
  `6fe7-956f-4901-45cf` (BigInt serialization), named in this ticket as candidate 2 — it is
  CLOSED and is a different mechanism (see rejection below). No sibling to resume.
- Reported-against floor: `created_at` 1787858559072112001 ns → main at/before 2026-08-25.
  Behaviour reproduced on today's `origin/main` (afe01efaa8b2), so the floor is not material.

### Discriminating experiment — the deployed endpoint, today

Unfiltered `tools/call list_tickets {}` against `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp`
(Streamable HTTP, bearer auth):

    http=200  size=94541551  time=177.286450

**The server did not fail.** It returned a well-formed JSON-RPC result of
**94,541,551 bytes (94.5 MB) over 177 seconds**, in one SSE `event: message` frame.

That single observation separates all three candidate causes:

1. **Response size — CONFIRMED.** 94.5 MB in one response, 177 s wall.
2. **BigInt serialization — REJECTED.** The call completed and the payload parses; the
   js-safe guard (`src/rebar/_mcp_errors.py:152` `js_safe_result`) is doing its job.
3. **Deploy cutover — REJECTED.** Reproducible on demand three days after the 18:54:29Z
   cutover, from a session that was never orphaned.

So the transport close is the **client** abandoning a 94.5 MB / 177 s single response, and it
is client-dependent: Copilot CLI reports `Transport closed`; this Claude Code session's own
config carries a 30 s connect budget (`claude mcp get rebar` → "connection timed out after
30000ms"); a third client succeeded but had to spill 219,815 chars to disk. The server offers
no bound and no structured signal, so none of them can distinguish "too big" from "server died".

### The changeable artifact

**The MCP read surface has exactly one payload bound and `list_tickets` is not wired to it.**

- `src/rebar/mcp_server.py:449-494` — `_WORKFLOW_TOKEN_BUDGET_BYTES = 90_000` and
  `_cap_workflow_payload()`, whose own comment states the contract: *"Keep MCP … payloads
  under the client's ~25K-token budget (WS-ffc4)."*
- It is applied to **two** tools only: `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:539` (`get_workflow_status`)
  and `:553` (`get_workflow_result`).
- `list_tickets` (`src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:278-326`) returns
  `[TicketStateOut.model_validate(t) for t in rebar.list_tickets(...)]` with **no size check
  at all**. Same for `ready_tickets`, `search`, `next_batch`.

### Why "lean by default" does not save it (question 3)

`list_tickets`' docstring claims *"lean by default — the bulky `description` and `comments`
fields are omitted so a broad list stays small"*. The claim is **literally true and materially
false**. `src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:494-496` is the whole lean path:

    if not include_body:
        ps.pop("description", None)
        ps.pop("comments", None)

Measured against the real store (2,855 tickets), lean vs full is 44.4 MB vs 73.0 MB — a 39%
saving that leaves the actual bulk untouched. Aggregate field weights of the **lean** payload:

| field | bytes | share of lean |
|---|---:|---:|
| `authorship_ledger` | 26,241,422 | 59% |
| `attestations` | 10,370,251 | 23% |
| `signature` | 2,639,114 | 6% |
| everything else | 5,141,280 | 12% |

**88% of the "lean" payload is base64 DSSE signature material** that a list caller never asked
for. Per row: 15,548 bytes lean; 1,726 bytes with those four fields (incl. `keyring`) dropped —
a 9x difference. The reported 10-row filtered call reproduces exactly: `tag=mcp, status=open,
type=bug` → 52,854 bytes lean, 11,178 bytes slim.

The mirror lean path in `src/rebar/_snapshot/ticket_view.py:383` has the same two-field drop.

### Legitimacy

This is a defect, not a misunderstanding: the behaviour diverges from two in-repo authoritative
statements — the `list_tickets` docstring's "stays small", and `_cap_workflow_payload`'s stated
"under the client's ~25K-token budget" contract that the rest of the read surface ignores.

## Phase 2 — fix pushed for review: Gerrit change 2336

`https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2336` — "Bound the MCP list read surface".
NOT submitted; `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` still pending.

### What changed

**1. The list surface is now BOUNDED, and refuses rather than truncates.**
`src/rebar/_mcp_budget.py` (new) holds the payload-budget cluster lifted out of
`mcp_server.py` — a real call-graph seam: both bounds measure through `_payload_bytes`,
and `mcp_server.py` had reached the 800-LOC hard cap. Alongside the existing
`_cap_workflow_payload` it adds `_bound_list_payload`, which reuses the SAME
`_WORKFLOW_TOKEN_BUDGET_BYTES` (90,000) and, when a list exceeds it, raises a `RebarError`
carrying the new `error_code="response_too_large"`. The already-installed
`install_error_guard` converts that into the standard rebar MCP envelope, so the caller
gets:

    {"error": "response_too_large", "message": "list_tickets matched 4000 tickets and
     would return 518902 bytes, over the 90000-byte MCP response budget. No partial list
     is returned (a short list cannot be told from a complete one). Narrow the query with
     one of status, ticket_type, priority, parent, has_tag, without_tag -- or read a
     single ticket with show_ticket.", "exit_code": 1}

Deliberately NOT the truncate-and-flag treatment a workflow payload gets: a shortened list
is indistinguishable from a complete one, which is the vacuous-result mode this project
refuses. Wired into `list_tickets` AND `ready_tickets` (both named in the AC).

**2. "Lean" is now actually lean.** `LEAN_OMITTED_FIELDS` + `lean_projection` in
`src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py` extend the `include_body=False` drop set from
`description`/`comments` to also drop `authorship_ledger`, `attestations`, `signature`,
`keyring`. The snapshot backend (`_snapshot/ticket_view.py`) calls the same function, so
the two read backends cannot drift.

### Why both halves were needed

| query | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| unfiltered (2,855) | 44,392,067 | 4,928,872 |
| per row | 15,548 | 1,726 |
| `status=open` (51) | 224,610 | 58,867 |
| `in_progress` (15) | 182,426 | 24,392 |
| `tag=mcp,status=open,type=bug` (10) | 52,854 | 11,178 |
| `ready` (61) | 693,556 | 76,878 |

Without the projection the 90 KB bound would refuse even `list_tickets(status="open")`.
With it, every ordinary query fits and only a genuinely unbounded one is refused.

### RED-first, mutation-checked

`tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_list_payload_budget.py` (7 tests) was written and seen
RED before any fix, driving the REGISTERED `CallToolRequest` handler a real client
reaches — not just `call_tool` — so a guard applied only to the post-`build_server()`
instance cannot pass it.

Mutation check, each half reverted independently:

- shrink `LEAN_OMITTED_FIELDS` back to the two body fields → **3 RED**
  (`lean=24072 full=24156: lean is not materially smaller`)
- neuter the budget comparison in `_bound_list_payload` → **3 RED**
  (`an over-budget list must not come back as a result`; `DID NOT RAISE ToolError`)
- restored → **7 GREEN**

### Gates

`make lint` (ruff check + format + complexity ratchet `active=39 new=0 increased=0`),
`make typecheck` (684 files clean), `pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`
(the extraction is what keeps `mcp_server.py` under the cap: 837 → 754),
`tests/unit` + `tests/interfaces` — 16,375 passed after fixing the four ctx fixtures and
regenerating `api_surface_baseline.json` for the new error code.

### Still open

The **LIVE VALIDATION** criterion is NOT met and this ticket must stay open until it is:
the change is on Gerrit, not merged and not deployed. Evidence must be re-taken against
`https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp` after the mcp container redeploys.

## Phase 3 — remediating Gerrit 2336 (LLM-Review -1, Verified -1)

### CI root cause — NOT packaging, and not a flake

`golden-path (clean install)` failed in 52 s on the **end-to-end CLI probe**, one assertion:

    FAIL: show adds exactly comments+description+digest_freshness+inbound_deps+plan_review_health
      over lean list (got [... 'keyring', ... 'signature'], want [...])

`scripts/probe_rebar.py:552` asserts the EXACT symmetric difference between `rebar show`
and `rebar list` key sets, in both directions, as a drift detector. Widening
`LEAN_OMITTED_FIELDS` changed the **CLI `rebar list`** shape too — not just MCP — because
`list_states(include_body=False)` shares `lean_projection`. So the probe was correct and
the change was under-declared: a **third** surface narrowed. Reproduced locally
(141 passed / 1 failed), fixed, now 142 passed / 0 failed.

The probe's expectation is now derived rather than hardcoded — the show-only computed
fields plus the lean-dropped set INTERSECTED with what `show` actually emits — because
`authorship_ledger`/`attestations` materialise only once a ticket has signature material,
so an empty tracker's `show` carries neither. Mutation-checked: shrinking
`LEAN_OMITTED_FIELDS` back to the two body fields still fails the probe.

### Findings 1+2 — `ready_tickets` contract: **option (b)**, lean-by-default, documented

Chosen over (a) preserve-full-default and (c) bound-only. The deciding fact is that both
alternatives make the DEFAULT call **fail** on this store: 61 ready tickets weigh 693,556
bytes unprojected against a 90,000-byte budget. Turning a working-but-oversized call into
a hard refusal is a *larger* break than returning less, and (b) keeps the two discovery
surfaces agreeing on their default shape instead of disagreeing. `full=True` returns
exactly the previous bytes; `show_ticket` is untouched. Recorded as BREAKING (pre-1.0) in
`docs/release-notes.md` + `CHANGELOG.md`, with the CLI `list` narrowing declared alongside.

### Finding 4 — the budget measured the wrong bytes. Confirmed, and worse than reported.

The reviewer named one axis (`js_safe_result` quoting 19-digit ints). Measured at this
store's 2,855 rows, there are **two**, and the larger one was unnamed:

| stage | bytes | delta |
|---|---:|---:|
| raw reducer dicts (what the bound measured) | 552,772 | — |
| after `TicketStateOut.model_validate` | 1,526,327 | **+973,555** |
| after `js_safe_result` | 1,537,747 | +11,420 |

`TicketStateOut` DECLARES defaults, so `model_validate` **re-adds every field the lean
projection just dropped** as an explicit `null`/`[]`/`""`. Total under-estimate: **178%** —
the 90,000-byte budget was in truth passing ~250,000-byte payloads.

Fixed by measuring the post-validation, post-`js_safe_result` rows (new `_wire_bytes`);
call sites now bound AFTER `model_validate`. Two tests, both mutation-killed by a faithful
pre-fix revert: an exactness assertion (measured == what the client receives) and the
regression window — 250 plain rows measure 49,652 bytes raw (under budget) but reach the
client as 135,902 (51% over), so the pre-fix bound returned them.

### Finding 5 — snapshot projection now tested

Two tests in `tests/unit/test_pinned_ticket_view.py` against a REAL pinned view over a real
tracker: same query through both backends, identical key sets (kills "stops projecting"),
and `include_body=True` still carries the bodies on both (kills "projects unconditionally").
The "cannot drift" claim is now enforced rather than asserted.

### Finding 3

No plan-review attestation on this ticket; `review-plan` run to earn one. No `--force`.

comments.body:
## Phase 4 — supporting detail moved out of the description (P4 admission limit)

The description exceeded the 8,000-char plan-review admission cap. Per `P4`'s own remedy —
keep the problem, constraints and ACs in the description; move investigation narration into
comments — the measurement detail lives here.

### Why the "lean" default was not lean (the 88% figure)

Measured on this store, 2,855 tickets. Lean vs full: 44.4 MB vs 73.0 MB — a 39% saving that
leaves the bulk untouched. Aggregate field weights of the **lean** payload:

| field | bytes | share of lean |
|---|---:|---:|
| `authorship_ledger` | 26,241,422 | 59% |
| `attestations` | 10,370,251 | 23% |
| `signature` | 2,639,114 | 6% |
| everything else | 5,141,280 | 12% |

Per row: 15,548 bytes lean; 1,726 with those four (incl. `keyring`) dropped — 9x.

### Why the budget had to measure the wire payload, not the reducer rows

Sizing raw dicts under-estimates on two axes. At 2,855 rows:

| stage | bytes | delta |
|---|---:|---:|
| raw reducer dicts | 552,772 | — |
| after `TicketStateOut.model_validate` | 1,526,327 | +973,555 |
| after `js_safe_result` | 1,537,747 | +11,420 |

A 178% under-estimate: the 90,000-byte budget was in truth passing ~250,000-byte payloads.
The dominant axis is the model's DECLARED defaults being re-added after the lean projection
dropped them, not the 19-digit-int quoting.

### `ready_tickets` headroom, and why the budget was not inflated

After projection: 58-59 rows, 87,893-88,480 wire bytes against 90,000 — ~1.7% headroom,
~1,499 B/row, so roughly one more ready ticket makes the default call refuse. The budget is
deliberately not raised: it is the client's real constraint, and raising it moves the failure
back into the client where there is no structured signal. Instead the refusal is made useful.
`ready_tickets` takes only `sort` and `full` — no filter arguments — so a shared "narrow with
has_tag" message would name parameters it rejects; its refusal points at `next_batch(epic_id)`.

Follow-up filed: `lucky-egoistic-akitainu` (`0c99-8f2b-0de7-48f2`), linked `discovered_from`,
carrying the discovery-shaped-projection options (234 B/row via a new closed output model =
~384 rows; 801 B/row via further field narrowing within `TicketStateOut` = ~112 rows).

### Surfaces measured for the breaking-change note

CLI `rebar list --status closed`, 2,696 rows, same ticket in each run: 39 keys -> 35 (losing
exactly `authorship_ledger`, `attestations`, `signature`, `keyring`), 43,661,976 -> 4,747,485
bytes, 9.2x. `--full` restores all four plus the bodies (41 keys, 71,707,799 bytes).

## Phase 5 — blast radius of the lean projection, MEASURED (do not re-derive)

Plan-review round 6 blocked (`G1G2`) arguing that widening `LEAN_OMITTED_FIELDS` inside
`list_states` would silently strip `authorship_ledger`/`attestations`/`signature`/`keyring`
from three non-MCP consumers. **That scenario does NOT materialise.** Measured against this
store rather than reasoned about:

| caller | exact call | rows | the four signature fields |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `validate.py:67` (`_raw_tickets`) | `list_states(tracker)` — `query=None` | 2,863 | **PRESENT** |
| `next_batch.py:144` | `list_states(tracker, TicketQuery(status="open,in_progress"))` | 62 | **PRESENT** |
| `reads_cli.py:344` (CLI `list` arm) | `list_states(tracker, TicketQuery(include_body=False))` | 2,863 | **DROPPED** |

Mechanism: `TicketQuery.include_body` defaults to **`True`** (`ticket_query.py:52`), and
`list_states(tracker)` with `query=None` constructs a default `TicketQuery()`
(`reads.py:437`). Only a caller that explicitly passes `include_body=False` narrows.

**So the blast radius is exactly three surfaces, all already documented as breaking:** MCP
`list_tickets`, MCP `ready_tickets`, and CLI `rebar list`. `validate` and `next_batch` are
unaffected and need no `full=True` compensation.

### Round-6 advisories that are artifacts, not defects

Two `E4` advisories report that `LEAN_OMITTED_FIELDS` and `_mcp_reads._discovery_rows` "do not
exist anywhere in the repo". True at `origin/main`, which is what the reviewer reads; false
after the change. An AC that cites symbols the change CREATES cannot be verified by a reviewer
reading the pre-change tree — worth phrasing future ACs as "introduces X" rather than naming X
as if it exists.

### Plan-review history on this ticket (6 rounds, none forced)

| round | blocking | nature |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | `T1` — description contradicted sibling `unreal-milky-sloth` |
| 2 | 3 | ACs under-specified the implementation (`G1G2`/`G6`/`T8`) |
| 3 | 2 | **real bug**: `ready_tickets` refusal named filters it does not accept |
| 4 | 1 | `P4` — description 9,226 chars over the 8,000 cap |
| 5 | 1 | `G1G2` — MCP-tool vs library layer conflated in AC wording |
| 6 | 1 | `G1G2` — AC-2 edit locus + unenumerated consumers (this comment) |

`P4` structural signals never flagged oversize (`ac_items` 9 vs cap 25; `file_impact` 9 vs cap
30). The pressure is not item count — it is that AC-2 must carry a four-layer argument (one
shared function -> two backends -> library untouched -> applied at the MCP tool layer -> three
surfaces narrow -> three consumers do not) inside an 8,000-char cap. Rounds 5 and 6 both blocked
on that single AC, and at 7,678 chars there were 322 left, less than the enumeration round 6
asked for. That is why this work is being split A (projection) / B (bound), B depending on A.

## Extraction safety: every consumer of the budget cluster (moved out of the description, P4 cap)

The budget cluster (`_WORKFLOW_TOKEN_BUDGET_BYTES`, `_payload_bytes`,
`_cap_workflow_payload`) moves from `mcp_server.py` to `src/rebar/_mcp_budget.py`. The
plan-review gate correctly blocked an earlier revision for claiming "nothing else in the
server calls them" while scoping that check to `mcp_server.py` alone. The full consumer set,
enumerated by grepping the symbol names across the repo:

**Inside `mcp_server.py`** — the definitions themselves, plus
`cap_workflow_payload=_cap_workflow_payload` on the shared tool context (`:636`).

**Outside `mcp_server.py`, referencing the symbol on its namespace — these would break on a
bare move:**

| consumer | reference |
|---|---|
| `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py:98` | `cap_workflow_payload=ms._cap_workflow_payload` |
| `tests/unit/test_gen_mcp_reference.py:122` | `cap_workflow_payload=ms._cap_workflow_payload` |
| `tests/interfaces/facades/test_workflow_mcp_schema.py:36,43,67` | `from rebar.mcp_server import _cap_workflow_payload` |

**Through the tool context, not the namespace — unaffected either way:**
`_mcp_reads.py:250` binds `_cap_workflow_payload = ctx.cap_workflow_payload`, used at `:598`
and `:612` for `get_workflow_status` / `get_workflow_result`.

**Resolution: RE-EXPORT, not repoint.** `mcp_server.py` imports `_cap_workflow_payload`,
`_bound_list_payload` and `_LIST_TOKEN_BUDGET_BYTES` back into its own namespace, so all three
external consumers keep working **unedited** and `rebar.mcp_server._cap_workflow_payload`
stays a valid import path. Repointing them at `rebar._mcp_budget` was the alternative; it was
rejected because it enlarges the change for no benefit and breaks any out-of-tree caller using
the same path. The three files passing unedited is the evidence that the re-export holds.

## Auth precondition for live validation — corrected

An earlier revision described the deployed endpoint as behind "the OAuth gate". That is wrong:
`REBAR_MCP_AUTH_STRATEGIES=static`, i.e. per-client **static bearer PATs**
(`MCP_CLIENT_PAT_COPILOT` / `MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CODEX` / `MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLAUDE`, see
`docs/mcp-client-setup.md:25-27`), not an OAuth authorization-code flow. The contract is
unchanged — a valid bearer token is required and a `401`/`403` is a FAILED validation, not an
environment excuse — only the mechanism is named correctly.

comments.body:
## Phase 5 — split into a two-change stack; Gerrit 2355

`https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2355`, stacked on
`https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2354`. NOT submitted. Gerrit 2336, which
carried both halves, is marked WIP with a supersession note.

This ticket is now the BOUND alone. The projection is `resistant-constant-nurseshark`
(`98b8-5f08-1569-45cc`), linked `depends_on` and landing first as 2354.

### What landed on 2355

`src/rebar/_mcp_budget.py` (extracted from `mcp_server.py` at 797 of its 800-LOC cap, along the
existing `_payload_bytes` seam), `_bound_list_payload` on both list tools, the
`response_too_large` `RebarError` refusal riding `install_error_guard`, the wire-measurement fix
(`_wire_bytes` measures post-`model_validate` + post-`js_safe_result` rows), the per-tool remedy,
and the release notes recording the refusal as ADDITIVE rather than breaking.

### Two defects the gate caught that CI would have caught later, and one it caught that CI did

1. **Extraction consumers (BLOCKING, G1G2).** Three consumers reference
   `_cap_workflow_payload` on the `rebar.mcp_server` namespace from OUTSIDE that module and
   would break on a bare move. Resolved by RE-EXPORT, so none is edited. Inventory in the
   extraction-safety comment.
2. **Tool-context builders (BLOCKING, G1G2).** The bound reaches tool bodies as a ctx member, so
   `register_read_tools` raises `AttributeError` against any ctx lacking it. The split had
   updated five of the seven test fixtures; the gate named the two missing ones
   (`test_read_freshness_parity.py`, `test_plan_review_explain.py`) and CI independently
   confirmed with 8 failures on patch set 1. Both fixed; nine builders now carry it.
3. **`error_code` attachment (BLOCKING, T8).** `RebarError.__init__` has no `error_code`
   parameter — only `CommandError` sets one — so the plan's "carrying `error_code=...`" was
   under-specified. The code is attached POST-CONSTRUCTION on the instance, which is what
   `error_code_for` step 5 reads via `getattr`. The plan now says so.

Also corrected: the live-validation auth precondition said "the OAuth gate"; the deployment uses
per-client STATIC bearer PATs (`REBAR_MCP_AUTH_STRATEGIES=static`).

### Verification

Mutation check: neutering the budget comparison turns 5 budget tests RED. `make lint`
(`active=39 new=0 increased=0`), `make typecheck` (685 files), and the 11 affected test modules
122 passed on the rebased stack.

### A rebase hazard worth recording

comments.body:
## The THIRD under-estimate axis: FastMCP emits the result twice (measured)

The code review on patch set 5 raised this, and it is real and material. Probed directly
against the registered `CallToolRequest` handler with 2 bulky rows:

```
content_blocks=2  content_bytes=1020  structured_bytes=944  total/structured = 2.08x
```

A `CallToolResult` for a list tool carries **both** halves:

- `structuredContent` — the whole `{"result": [...]}` object; and
- one `content` text block **per row**, each serialized as `json.dumps(row, indent=2)`
  (confirmed exactly: a single block was 510 bytes, matching `indent=2` and neither the
  default `json.dumps` at 466 nor the compact separators at 425).

So a bound measuring only `structuredContent` passes a payload **~2.08x** the budget — the
same "passes something that still overruns" failure the other two axes cause, and the reason
the AC insists the measurement be the wire payload. `_wire_bytes` now counts both halves.

### The regression test was a convergence twin; it no longer is

The exactness assertion previously compared `_wire_bytes(models)` against
`json.dumps({"result": js_safe_result(models)})` — a second spelling of the function's own
arithmetic, so it would have passed however wrong both sides were, and it did pass while the
measurement was 2x low. The oracle is now the **real emitted `CallToolResult`**, obtained by
running the tool and summing every `content` block plus `structuredContent`.

Mutation-checked both ways: neutering the budget comparison turns 6 tests RED; reverting
`_wire_bytes` to measure only `structuredContent` is caught by the exactness assertion
(measured 10,862 vs 22,632 actually emitted).

## `search` is the third discovery list, and it was unbounded

`search`'s docstring opens *"Search titles/descriptions/comments/tags with **bounded**
discovery results"* — but the tool had no size check at all, only the narrower
`project_search_result` row shape making an ordinary query small. An unfiltered one was as
unbounded as `list_tickets`. It now shares the same bound, with its own remedy naming what it
can actually narrow with (a more specific query, a field predicate, or its
`status`/`ticket_type`/`has_tag` arguments) — never `ready_tickets`' `next_batch` pointer,
which would be wrong for a tool that does take filters.

compiled_state.description:
## The problem, and its proven root cause

`list_tickets` here can terminate with `MCP request failed: Transport closed` and no structured
error payload — the caller cannot tell an invalid query from a dead server from a too-large
response. Unfiltered `tools/call list_tickets {}` against the deployed endpoint
returned `http=200`, **94,541,551 bytes over 177.29 seconds**, in one well-formed SSE frame:
**the server does not fail**, the client abandons that response in a client-specific way, and
none can tell "too big" from "server died" because the server offers no bound and no structured
signal. Rejected candidates and the measurements are in the Phase 1 / Phase 4 comments.

## Scope: this ticket is the BOUND; the projection is its prerequisite

`resistant-constant-nurseshark` (`98b8-5f08-1569-45cc`) is the lean projection, linked
`depends_on` and **must land first**: without it this bound would refuse even
`list_tickets(status="open")` at 224,610 lean bytes. Not greenfield — `_cap_workflow_payload`
already states this 90,000-byte contract (WS-ffc4) but is wired to the two workflow reads only;
the discovery lists have **no size check at all**.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Cause identified and reconciled with both sibling tickets (above).

- [ ] **All THREE discovery lists bound at one budget, and REFUSE rather than truncate.**
      `list_tickets`, `ready_tickets` and `search` bound at `_LIST_TOKEN_BUDGET_BYTES`, aliasing
      the existing 90,000-byte `_WORKFLOW_TOKEN_BUDGET_BYTES` rather than adding a second
      number. `search` is included because its docstring already promised "bounded discovery
      results" while having no size check. No partial list is returned: a short list is
      indistinguishable from a complete one. **Verified by** a per-tool test asserting an
      over-budget call returns no result and no `structuredContent`.

- [ ] **The budget measures the WIRE payload, not the reducer rows — on all THREE axes.** An
      under-estimating bound passes something that still overruns, so the bound runs INSIDE the
      tool body after `TicketStateOut.model_validate` and calls `js_safe_result` itself rather
      than waiting for the error guard, which applies that transform only after the body
      returns. (1) Model defaults re-added after the projection and (2) JS-safe int quoting
      under-report by 178% together; (3) **FastMCP emits the result TWICE** —
      `structuredContent` PLUS one `content` block per row — **2.08x** the structured object
      alone (figures in the comment). **Verified by** an exactness assertion whose oracle is
      the REAL emitted `CallToolResult`, never a second spelling of the bound's arithmetic —
      that would be a convergence twin, and the previous version was one.

- [ ] **The refusal is structured, and the exception TYPE is right.** Raises a
      `rebar._errors.RebarError`. The TYPE matters, not just the attribute: `_envelope_error`
      envelopes only a known rebar exception type, so a plain `Exception` with `.error_code` is
      dropped and the caller gets an unstructured failure. **`RebarError.__init__` has no
      `error_code` parameter** (only `CommandError` sets one), so the code is attached
      POST-CONSTRUCTION — `err.error_code = "response_too_large"` on the instance before the
      raise — which is what `error_code_for` step 5 reads via `getattr`. No change to
      `error_code_for`, no schema change (`error_envelope.error` is an open string); the code
      joins `rebar.KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` + `tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json`. **Verified by**
      a test asserting the raised `ToolError`'s `__cause__` is an `McpEnvelopeError` whose
      envelope names that code — which fails if the attribute never lands — plus the baseline.

- [ ] **The remedy is one the REFUSED TOOL can execute.** `list_tickets` names its six filters.
      **`ready_tickets` accepts NO filter argument** — only `sort` and the `full` its
      prerequisite adds, and `full` switches SHAPE, not membership — so a shared "narrow with
      has_tag" message would name arguments the tool rejects. Its refusal points at
      `next_batch(epic_id)`, while `search` names a more specific query, a field predicate or
      its `status`/`ticket_type`/`has_tag` arguments. The remedy has to work: `ready_tickets`
      sits at ~1.7% headroom
      after the projection (59 rows, 88,480 of 90,000 bytes), and the budget is NOT inflated to
      hide that, since raising it moves the failure back into the client where there is no
      structured signal (follow-up: `lucky-egoistic-akitainu` / `0c99-8f2b-0de7-48f2`). **Verified by** a test asserting `list_tickets`' message names its
      filters and `ready_tickets`' names `next_batch` and NOT
      `has_tag`/`without_tag`/`parent`.

- [ ] **The extraction preserves every consumer.** The cluster moves to
      `src/rebar/_mcp_budget.py` (a real call-graph seam — both bounds measure through
      `_payload_bytes`; `mcp_server.py` is at 797 of its 800-LOC cap). **Three consumers
      reference `_cap_workflow_payload` on the `rebar.mcp_server` namespace from OUTSIDE that
      module and would break on a bare move**: `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py:98`,
      `tests/unit/test_gen_mcp_reference.py:122`,
      `tests/interfaces/facades/test_workflow_mcp_schema.py:36,43,67`. All are preserved by
      **RE-EXPORT**, not repointed, so none is edited (alternative rejected in the
      extraction-safety comment). **Verified by** those three passing unedited plus
      `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`.

- [ ] **Every builder of the shared tool context gains `bound_list_payload`.** The bound reaches
      tool bodies as a ctx member, so `register_read_tools` raises `AttributeError` against any
      ctx lacking it — an omitted builder fails at REGISTRATION, not assertion. NINE exist and
      ALL are updated: `mcp_server.build_server`, `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py`, and
      seven `tests/unit` fixtures (`test_audit_read`, `test_bridge_projects_surfaces_heldout`,
      `test_cross_session_mcp`, `test_gen_mcp_reference`, `test_mcp_plan_review_status`,
      `test_plan_review_explain`, `test_read_freshness_parity`). **Verified by** running each.

- [ ] **Regression coverage asserts the error's CONTENTS**, not merely that a refusal occurred:
      `error` as its own envelope key, and match count, byte size, budget and remedy as
      substrings WITHIN `message`, for BOTH tools. Plus an under-budget list returned whole,
      and the regression window: 250 plain rows measuring 49,652 raw (under budget) but far
      more on the wire must still be refused. Driven through the REGISTERED `CallToolRequest`
      handler a real client reaches, so a guard on the post-`build_server()` instance cannot
      pass. **Verified by** a mutation check: neutering the comparison turns these RED.

- [ ] **LIVE VALIDATION — REQUIRED TO CLOSE.** `list_tickets` and `ready_tickets` through the
      deployed endpoint return results (or a structured limit error) with no transport close.
      **Auth precondition:** the endpoint uses per-client **static bearer PATs**
      (`REBAR_MCP_AUTH_STRATEGIES=static`, `MCP_CLIENT_PAT_*` per `docs/mcp-client-setup.md`),
      NOT OAuth, so the client MUST send `Authorization: Bearer $MCP_CLIENT_PAT_…`; a
      `401`/`403` is a FAILED validation, not an environment excuse. Evidence must be OBSERVED against the deployed
      server and recorded in a comment naming the tools, arguments and response. Neither a local test nor a merged change satisfies this: the container
      must have redeployed and served the call.

## Definition of Done

- `docs/release-notes.md` + `CHANGELOG.md` record the refusal as NEW behaviour.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean; `pytest tests/unit tests/interfaces` no failures.
- `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` on Gerrit, stacked on the prerequisite.
- Live-validation evidence recorded as a comment on this ticket.
